newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak govt says c.bank supports bank sell-off.
newsitem.headline: Slovak govt says c.bank supports bank sell-off.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) has approved a resolution supporting the completion of bank privatisation, a government spokeswoman said on Tuesday.

"Governor (Vladimir) Masar, at the beginning of today's regular government meeting, informed the cabinet that the NBS governing board last Friday approved a document in which it approved and supported the completion of bank privatisation," Magda Pospisilova told journalists.

On February 13, Slovak parliament approved a measure adding the four state-controlled financial institutions to a list of strategic companies, effectively halting the bank sell-off by the end of the year 2003 at the earliest.

Pospisilova said Masar stressed there was no political influence on the board, and that the move was taken "purely on technical grounds." She would not elaborate further. NBS officials were not immediately available for comment.

The Slovak government has said it is considering asking President Michal Kovac not to sign the law barring the sell-off. The law was not supported by Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar's ruling Movement for a Democratic Slovakia (HZDS).
The government is scheduled to discuss materials giving technical grounds for returning the law to parliament for re-assessment at its session later on Wednesday.

According to the Slovak constitution, the president must return a law to the parliament at the request of the government. A law becomes effective when it is signed by both the prime minister and president.

Through the NPF, the state controls 91.3 percent of the largest savings bank Slovenska Sporitelna, 50.5 percent if insurer Slovenska Poistovna, some 35 percent in bank IRB and about 17 percent in the largest commercial bank VUB.
The Czech National Property Fund also holds about 33 percent in VUB.

Deputy Foreign Minister Jozef Sestak told the news conference that postponement of bank privatisation could delay Slovakia's integration in the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD), expected to be completed by the end of this year.
"Bank privatisation is one of the crucial conditions for Slovakia's entry in the OECD and postponement may have negative influence on our integration," Sestak said.
Delays in the bank sell-offs could endanger further restructuring of the entire economy, he added.
"Though membership in the OECD remains one of the top priorities the government cannot bear political responsibility in the case of postponement of bank privatisation," Sestak said.

Political and economic analysts say the current row over banking privatisation inside the coalition may indicate a serious crisis between the coalition partners after one of its members voted together with the opposition in support of the law.

Opposition parties and the ultra-left Workers Party (ZRS), who defected from the coalition in the vote, said they would again vote for the postponement of bank privatisation if the government uses its right to ask the president to return the law to parliament.
